modules.title: Module 1 · Angles in a Circle
modules.html:
1. Angle at centre is twice the angle at circumference subtended by the same arc.
  2. Angles in the same segment are equal.
  3. Angle in a semicircle is a right angle ($90°$).

Key points

  • Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180°$: $\angle C = 180° - 125° = 55°$.
  • Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180°$: $\angle C = 180° - 88° = 92°$.

Worked example

Q: In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle A = 125°$. Find $\angle C$.
A: 55°

Q: In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle A = 88°$. Find $\angle C$.
A: 92°

More key points

  • Two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn from an external point $P$ to a circle. If $PA = 7$ cm, find $PB$. — 7 cm.
  • Two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn from an external point $P$ to a circle. If $PA = 19$ cm, find $PB$. — 19 cm.
  • Two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn from an external point $P$ to a circle. If $PA = 9$ cm, find $PB$. — 9 cm.
  • Two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn from an external point $P$ to a circle. If $PA = 18$ cm, find $PB$. — 18 cm.

modules.title: Module 2 · Cyclic Quadrilaterals
modules.html:
A quadrilateral whose vertices lie on a circle. Its opposite angles are supplementary: $A + C = 180°$ and $B + D = 180°$. The exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.

Key points

  • Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180°$: $\angle C = 180° - 125° = 55°$.
  • Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180°$: $\angle C = 180° - 88° = 92°$.

Worked example

Q: In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle A = 125°$. Find $\angle C$.
A: 55°

Q: In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle A = 88°$. Find $\angle C$.
A: 92°

More key points

  • In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle A = 125°$. Find $\angle C$. — 55°.
  • In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle A = 88°$. Find $\angle C$. — 92°.
  • In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle A = 103°$. Find $\angle C$. — 77°.
  • In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle A = 106°$. Find $\angle C$. — 74°.

modules.title: Module 3 · Tangent Properties
modules.html:
• A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
  • Two tangents from an external point are equal in length.
  • Alternate segment theorem: the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment.

Key points

  • A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency.

Worked example

Q: What is the angle between a tangent and the radius drawn to the point of contact?
A: 90°

More key points

  • What is the angle between a tangent and the radius drawn to the point of contact — 90°.

modules.title: Angle properties of circles
modules.html:
Angle properties of circles is a key part of Circle Theorems (SSS 2, Mathematics). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Angle at centre is twice the angle at circumference subtended by the same arc.
  • Angles in the same segment are equal.
  • Angle in a semicircle is a right angle ($90°$).
  • Key points Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180°$: $\angle C = 180° - 125° = 55°$.
  • Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180°$: $\angle C = 180° - 88° = 92°$.

Worked example

Q: An arc subtends an angle of $110°$ at the centre. What angle does it subtend at the circumference?
A: 55° — Angle at centre is twice the angle at the circumference: $110° \div 2 = 55°$.

Q: An arc subtends an angle of $140°$ at the centre. What angle does it subtend at the circumference?
A: 70° — Angle at centre is twice the angle at the circumference: $140° \div 2 = 70°$.

modules.html:
Revise the whole topic by working through its key points in order, then test yourself with the 50-question quiz for this topic. Pay attention to definitions, differences between similar terms, and questions that ask you to apply the topic rather than only recall it.

quiz.q: Calculate the area of a circle of radius 7cm (Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$).
